newsitem.title: FINLAND: 20,000 Finns jig for prize trout on frozen lake.
newsitem.headline: 20,000 Finns jig for prize trout on frozen lake.

text.p: Over 20,000 people huddled for hours over small holes in a frozen Finnish lake on Saturday, angling for a single trout worth $250,000.
The annual Finnish jigging, or ice-fishing, contest is held in sub-zero temperatures on a lake near the western village of Tuuri, Finnish for "luck".
The specially marked trout, weighing over seven kg (15lb), is one of 10,000 organisers released into the lake last autumn.
"People are really going for the big fish," organiser Juhani Kauppinen said by telephone. "They're having a great time."
Earlier on Saturday, Norwegian Tommy Strengelsvud caught over 28 kg (62 lbs) of trout in five and a half hours to claim the title of ice-fishing world-champion, Kauppinen said.
But the Finnish event held a catch of another kind: the prize money comes in vouchers valid only in a local shop.
